newsitem.title: USA: Compaq says is committed to distributors.
newsitem.headline: Compaq says is committed to distributors.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp said Monday that while it does not comment on rumors about acquisitions, it said it does evaluate all opportunties relating to its business and that ultimately, it remains committed to working with its current computer resellers and distributors.

Compaq issued its statement in response to a report in Time Magazine, which said that the world's largest PC maker almost merged with Gateway 2000 Inc, but that the deal fell apart at the last minute. Gateway is a direct seller of PCs and Compaq sells through distributors and resellers.
A Gateway spokeswoman declined to comment on the report.

"Compaq is approached by and entertains discussions with many companies who would like to merge or partner with Compaq," said Dick Synder, a Compaq senior vice president, in a statement. "We evaluate all opportunities relative to our business and for the customer. Ultimately, we have determined that the customer and the business are best served by a strong highly-competitive channel model."
Compaq said through its relationship with its channel partners, it is driving toward a customer delivery model that will be the most efficient, effective and cost competitive in the industry.

"Compaq's focus and investment on build-to-order and configure-to-order will yield efficient, cost competitive distribution of leading edge products through a proven channel of information technology experts," Snyder said. "And that is far more dramatic than any of this other speculation."
